name: Stew Calls Gallagher
description: Stew picks up the phone and dials Gallagher. The line connects, and he says, 'Hello, Gallagher old pal. How are you, old pal?'
related_events: Stew makes a telephone call to Gallagher

name: Stew Enters the Drawing Room
description: Stew, wearing a business suit, walks down the stairs and moves down the hallway toward the drawing room. He stops just short of the door, listening to the silence coming from inside. He glances toward the front door, then turns back to the drawing room, straightens his shoulders, and steps inside.
related_events: Stew prepares to enter the drawing room after pausing in the hallway

name: Anne Coordinates Evening Plans During Massage
description: Anne lies on her stomach on a massage table, a Swedish masseuse working on her back with firm, rhythmic strokes. The sound of each press and rub fills the room, punctuated by the occasional snap of the therapist’s hands. Anne holds a telephone to her ear, speaking in a calm but insistent tone. She tells her partner it is nearly six o'clock and reminds them how long it takes to get ready. She mentions the Ambassador is due to arrive at eight, and stresses that they must be ready by the time he gets there.
related_events: Anne discusses evening preparations with partner over phone
Masseuse performs massage on Anne's back

name: Footmen Receive Guests at Estate Entrance
description: Two footmen stand at either side of a large iron gate as cars and limousines arrive, one after another. Guests dressed in evening wear step out and are greeted at the entrance to the estate. The footmen remain in place, acknowledging each arrival as the evening gathering begins.
related_events: footmen stand at attention at the iron gate
guests arrive at the estate entrance in cars and limousines
related_occasions: Evening Social Gathering At The Estate

name: Stew Apologizes to Gallagher in the Ballroom
description: Gallagher enters the ballroom when Stew hurries after her. He calls out, apologizing for Anne's behavior and expressing that he's truly sorry. Gallagher turns to him, assuring him it's all right and telling him to forget about it, adding that as far as Anne is concerned, she's just part of the hired help. Stew insists he's never seen Anne act that way before, pauses, and remarks that it's strange he never thought to tell her Gallagher was a girl. Gallagher agrees, saying it is funny.
related_events: Stew apologizes to Gallagher for Anne's behavior
Gallagher reassures Stew about being treated as hired help
Stew reflects on not telling Anne that Gallagher is a woman

name: Bingy Examines the Vase and Stew Teases Him
description: Bingy rises from his throne chair and walks into the library, stopping at a carved low-boy where a large antique vase sits. He studies it closely, turning it slightly in his hands. Stew enters the room, sees Bingy at the low-boy, and pauses with a smile. He approaches and says, 'What's the matter, Bingy, a little clumsy to get in your pocket?' Bingy sets the vase down and looks at him. 'No. I was just looking at it. Pretty, ain't it? I was just looking for the price tag.'
related_events: Bingy examines an antique vase in the library
Stew enters and observes Bingy at the vase
Stew makes a joking remark about the vase
Bingy responds to Stew's comment about the vase

name: Grayson Confronts Anne Over Her Absence and Plans for Stew
description: Dexter Grayson approaches Anne, standing in her evening gown with a cocktail and cigarette in hand, and demands to know where she was the previous day. Anne gazes into the distance and replies that she took a long ride with Stew, then casually muses about sending him to a finishing school. Grayson responds with sharp sarcasm, suggesting Sing Sing would be a more fitting destination. Anne dismisses his comment, stating with confidence that Stew will become a different person under her influence. Grayson stares at her, skeptical, and repeats her words with disbelief. She calls it an interesting experiment. He sneers, asking if she intends to make a gentleman out of a tramp. Unmoved, Anne says this man is different—he has brains. Grayson reminds her of the emotional and financial cost they paid during their last entanglement, implying the same mistake could happen again.
related_events: Dexter Grayson confronts Anne about her absence
Anne describes her ride with Stew and suggests a finishing school
Dexter Grayson reacts with sarcastic suggestion of Sing Sing
Anne confidently asserts her influence will change Stew
Dexter Grayson expresses incredulity at Anne's plan
Dexter Grayson warns of emotional and financial costs from past experience

name: The Gang Takes Over the Residence
description: The gang spreads out through the residence, lounging across furniture and idly strumming the piano. Some wander the room, looking around with wide eyes and quiet amazement. Others guide Smythe in uneven circles, pushing him along as he protests. He shakes his head, muttering sharply, 'It isn't done, gentlemen! It isn't done, I say! It isn't done!'
related_events: Gang members make themselves at home in the residence
Gang members play the piano and inspect the room

name: Smythe is pushed around the room by revellers
description: The gang drapes themselves across the room, some strumming the piano while others look around in awe. A few of them grab hold of Smythe and push him around the space as he resists. He protests loudly, insisting their behavior is improper, but they continue to move him against his will.
related_events: Revellers forcibly move Smythe around the room
Smythe protests the gang's behavior

name: Gallagher Takes Stew's Call from Norway
description: Gallagher stands in a simple room, likely in a boarding house or cheap hotel, speaking on the phone. A typewriter sits nearby. She greets Stew and asks how he is. Stew tells her he is on the coast of Norway and cannot get out, asking her to come and get him. Gallagher responds by remarking on his play, noting that it only has 'Act One, Scene One: Coast of Norway' and then nothing else. Stew urges her to act, suggesting she bring Hank if she needs company, saying Hank would be a perfect bodyguard. He expresses confidence in her, and Gallagher agrees. After hanging up, she smiles, clearly pleased at the prospect of seeing Stew, and hums softly as she picks up the phone again.
related_events: Gallagher speaks with Stew on the telephone
Stew requests rescue from the coast of Norway
Gallagher comments on the sparse content of Stew's play

name: Gallagher Prepares to Contact Hank at Joe's
description: After hanging up the phone, Gallagher hums softly, a lightness in her movements. She picks up the receiver again, ready to call Joe's, searching for Hank.
related_events: Stew suggests Gallagher call Hank for companionship
Gallagher prepares to contact Hank after Stew's suggestion

name: Stew Reacts to Bingy's Arrival at the Reception
description: The butler approaches Stew and Gallagher, informing Stew that Bingy is at the reception. Stew turns to Gallagher and says he needs to make sure Bingy doesn’t take any of the vases. As he starts to walk away, he stops, turns back, and looks at Gallagher with surprise. 'Well, well, well! My little pal, Gallagher, a girl, huh?' Without warning, he bends down and kisses her hand. 'That's just to give you an idea that I know how to treat a gal,' he says softly. Then, straightening up, he adds, 'Get fresh with me and I'll sock you in that little nose of yours.' He leaves. Gallagher remains behind, staring at her hand in quiet astonishment.
related_events: Butler informs Stew of Bingy's presence at the reception
Stew leaves to check on the vases at the reception

name: Stew Kisses Gallagher's Hand and Threatens Her
description: Stew turns to Gallagher after speaking with the butler, who has just informed him that Bingy is at the reception. 'Excuse me. I just want to make sure and see he doesn't take away any of the vases,' he says, starting to leave. He stops, turns back, and looks at her with a smirk. 'Well, well, well! My little pal, Gallagher, a girl, huh?' Without warning, he bends down and kisses her hand. 'That's just to give you an idea that I know how to treat a gal,' he says softly. Then, his tone shifts. 'Get fresh with me and I'll sock you in that little nose of yours.' He walks away, leaving Gallagher standing still, staring at her hand.
related_events: Stew threatens Gallagher after complimenting her

name: Stew and Gallagher Talk About the Play
description: Stew and Gallagher enter the room, continuing a conversation about Stew's play. Stew mentions he has just managed to get off the Norway coast in his writing. He gestures toward the typewriter with a sheet of paper sticking out. Gallagher walks over, rolls up the page, and reads aloud: 'Act One - Scene One - A Street in Old Madrid.' She turns to Stew with a smile and remarks that while he isn't making much progress on the play, he is certainly covering a lot of ground. Stew grins and agrees, saying it feels like he's been on a Cook's Tour. She asks if he's ever been to Old Madrid. Stew looks confused and asks what she means. Gallagher repeats the question. Stew admits he's never even been to New Madrid. She challenges him, asking how he expects to write about a place he's never seen. Stew says he supposes he'll have to use his imagination. Gallagher brings up Conrad, asking if he used imagination too. Stew is startled, asking who she means. When she clarifies it's Conrad, Stew asks what she knows about him. She says she doesn't know anything, but points out that he's always talking about Conrad, who only writes about things he knows from experience. Stew acknowledges she's right. Gallagher suggests he write about something he knows—himself and Anne. She proposes the story of a poor boy marrying a rich girl as a strong theme. Stew warms to the idea, excitedly adding characters: Anne's mother, the lawyer, and Gallagher herself. He rushes to the typewriter, asking her to get him a cigarette. She hands it to him. He starts thinking out loud about how to begin, asking her for suggestions.
related_events: Stew and Gallagher discuss progress on Stew's play
Gallagher reads the opening scene of Stew's play
Gallagher compliments Stew's creative reach despite lack of progress

name: Gallagher Questions Stew's Approach to Writing
description: Stew and Gallagher enter the room, continuing a conversation about his play. Stew mentions he has made progress, having moved his story from the Norway coast to a street in Old Madrid. He gestures toward the typewriter with a page still in it. Gallagher walks over, rolls up the page, and reads aloud: 'Act One - Scene One - A Street in Old Madrid.' She smiles and remarks that while he may not be finishing his play, he is certainly covering a lot of ground. Stew grins and agrees, saying it feels like he’s been on a Cook's Tour. Gallagher turns serious and asks if he’s ever been to Old Madrid. Stew admits he’s never even been to New Madrid. She challenges him, asking how he expects to write about a place he’s never seen. Stew replies that he supposes he’ll draw on his imagination. Gallagher counters by asking if Conrad used imagination, pointing out that Stew often talks about Conrad writing only from experience. Stew is taken aback. Gallagher reminds him that Conrad went to sea before writing about it. Stew falls quiet, then says, 'Gee, that's an idea, Gallagher.' She suggests he write about something he knows—himself and Anne, the story of a poor boy marrying a rich girl. Stew warms to the idea, excitedly imagining characters based on Anne’s mother, her lawyer friend, and even Gallagher herself. He rushes to the typewriter, asking her to hand him a cigarette as he prepares to begin writing.
related_events: Gallagher challenges Stew's use of imagination over experience
Stew reacts to Gallagher's insight about Conrad

name: Stew Finds Inspiration in Real Life
description: Gallagher suggests that Stew write about his relationship with Anne, pointing out that he could draw from his own experiences. Stew listens, then begins to imagine the people in his life as characters in a play—Anne, her mother, her lawyer friend, and even Gallagher. His excitement grows as he envisions the possibilities. He puts an arm around Gallagher’s shoulder, then suddenly rushes to the typewriter. He sits down, ready to begin, and asks Gallagher to hand him a cigarette. After she gives it to him, he leans forward, thinking aloud about how to start, and turns to her, asking for her help with the opening lines.
related_events: Gallagher suggests Stew write about his relationship with Anne
Stew becomes inspired by the idea of writing about his life with Anne
Stew rushes to the typewriter to begin writing
Stew asks Gallagher for help in starting the play

name: The Delayed Departure
description: The formal reception at the Schuyler home had run past its scheduled end, and the butler, Smythe, approached Mrs. Schuyler to inform her that the Mayor's committee had called with a reminder. Mrs. Schuyler turned to inquire whether the cars were ready. Smythe replied that they had been waiting for the past half hour.
related_events: Butler informs Mrs. Schuyler about the Mayor's committee reminder
Mrs. Schuyler inquires about the readiness of the cars
Butler reports that the cars have been waiting for half an hour

name: Anne Goes to Check on Her Husband
description: A lady in the group remarks that it is growing late and wonders what is causing the delay. Anne replies that they are waiting for her husband, then excuses herself and walks upstairs toward Stew's room.
related_events: A lady in the group comments on the late hour and delays
Anne reveals they are waiting for her husband and excuses herself
Anne heads upstairs toward Stew's room to check on her husband

name: Anne and Captain White's Playful Exchange
description: Captain White stood among the guests, dressed in his aviator's uniform, and admitted to Anne that he was nervous about giving another speech that evening. Anne smiled and teased him, saying that women were eager to see a celebrated round-the-world flier, a rare sight indeed. He confessed that such attention made him uneasy and joked that this was already the fourth dinner she had taken him to in just one week—he was beginning to run out of things to say. She playfully asked if he was complaining. Before he could answer, another guest remarked on the lateness of the hour, wondering what was keeping them. Anne replied lightly that they were waiting for her husband, then excused herself and walked up the stairs toward Stew's room.
related_events: Captain White expresses nervousness about speaking at the evening event
Anne teases Captain White about his celebrity status
Captain White jokes about attending multiple dinners with Anne in one week
Anne playfully questions Captain White if he is complaining about the dinners

name: Stew and Anne Enter the Garden and Move to the Pergola
description: Stew and Anne enter the garden from the direction of the house, their hands clasped together. The garden is dimly lit, with only a soft glow spilling from the house behind them. They walk slowly toward the edge of the vine-covered pergola, drawn to the gentle trickle of water flowing down a glass partition. Around them, rose trees are in bloom, marble statues stand in quiet repose, and a fountain splashes softly. They pass through the shadows and move behind the fountain, settling onto a low, deep divan, their figures now visible in silhouette against the faint light.
related_events: Stew and Anne enter the garden hand in hand
Stew and Anne walk to the edge of the pergola

name: Stew and Anne Embrace Behind the Fountain
description: Stew and Anne settle onto a low divan behind the dimly lit fountain, their figures outlined in silhouette against the soft glow from the house. The sound of water trickling down the glass partition blends with the distant melody of an Italian love song. Without hesitation, they fall into a passionate embrace, wrapped in the quiet intimacy of the garden.
related_events: Stew and Anne settle into the low divan behind the fountain
Stew and Anne share a passionate embrace in silhouette

name: Stew Confesses His Feelings, Anne Reassures Him
description: Stew and Anne sit close on a low divan behind the fountain, their figures in silhouette against the soft glow from the house. Water trickles down the glass partition nearby, and a distant Italian love song drifts through the garden. Overcome with emotion, Stew stammers through a halting confession, listing small personal details—his name, preferences, bank balance—ending with his uncertainty about the color of her eyes. Anne smiles, her gaze never leaving his. She reaches out and gently pinches his nose, telling him there’s no reason to leave, that they’re happy together. He insists, saying he’s getting goofy ideas about her. She replies, her voice soft and sure, that none of his ideas can be goofy if they’re about her. He turns to her, their eyes meet, and without another word, he pulls her into his arms and kisses her deeply.
related_events: Stew confesses his feelings and personal details to Anne on the divan
Anne gently pinches Stew's nose and reassures him of their happiness

name: Stew and Anne Share a Passionate Kiss
description: Stew stops speaking, overwhelmed. He pulls Anne close, wraps his arms around her, and kisses her deeply. She responds without hesitation, their embrace growing more intense as the sound of the fountain and the distant singing continue around them.
related_events: Stew abandons rationality and passionately kisses Anne

name: Breakfast Conversation About the Reception
description: Anne and her mother sit at the breakfast table. Anne greets her mother and brings up the previous night's reception, saying her husband was marvelous and that everyone found him charming. Mrs. Schuyler admits she had been worried he might knock over a vase or cause a scene, and feels she may have acted foolishly. She notices the morning paper in Anne's hands and asks what it says about the event. Anne flips through it, dismissing the coverage as repetitive and uninteresting. Mrs. Schuyler scolds her for being flippant, saying she sounds like her husband. Anne insists her mother has no reason to complain, pointing out that he behaved appropriately the night before. Mrs. Schuyler reluctantly agrees it was a miracle, adding that the man must have been ill. Then she sees the front page of the paper and lets out a scream, pointing at the headline. Anne turns the paper to see it. The headline reads: 'CINDERELLA MAN GROWS HAIR ON CHEST ATTACKS REPORTER IN SCHUYLER HOME. "I wear the pants," says Anne Schuyler's husband. "It's Okay with me," says Anne.' Mrs. Schuyler rises from the table, pacing frantically, repeating 'I knew it! I felt it in my bones!' Grayson rushes into the room, holding a copy of the paper, and demands if they've seen the story. Before he can continue, Mrs. Schuyler interrupts, saying she's already aware. Smythe the butler enters with a tray, and Mrs. Schuyler stammers, telling him to send for Mr. Smith, then corrects herself and tells Smythe to send for Mr. Smith. Smythe nods and says, 'Double-strength,' as he exits. Mrs. Schuyler mutters the headline under her breath as she leaves the room, with Grayson following close behind, scornfully repeating the quote: '"I wear the pants," says Anne Schuyler's husband!'
related_events: Anne and her mother discuss the previous night's reception over breakfast

name: Mrs. Schuyler Reacts to the Newspaper Headline
description: Mrs. Schuyler notices the front page of the morning paper in Anne's hands. Her expression turns to horror as she reads the headline. She lets out a piercing scream, startling Anne. 'Look! Look! The front page!' she cries, pointing frantically. Anne turns the paper toward herself and reads the article. The headline declares: 'CINDERELLA MAN GROWS HAIR ON CHEST ATTACKS REPORTER IN SCHUYLER HOME. "I wear the pants," says Anne Schuyler's husband. "It's Okay with me," says Anne.' Mrs. Schuyler rises from her seat, pacing the room in distress. 'I knew it! I knew it! I felt it in my bones!' she exclaims. Grayson bursts into the room, waving a copy of the same paper, demanding if they've seen the story. Before he can continue, Mrs. Schuyler interrupts, ordering the butler to send for Mr. Smith. As she mutters the headline under her breath, she exits the room in agitation, with Grayson following close behind, scornfully repeating the quote about wearing the pants.
related_events: Mrs. Schuyler reacts in horror to a newspaper headline
Anne reads the newspaper article about her husband's outburst

name: Mrs. Schuyler's Hysterical Reaction to the Newspaper Scandal
description: Mrs. Schuyler leaps from her seat and paces wildly around the room, crying out that she had known this disaster would happen, that she felt it in her bones. As Smythe the butler enters with a tray, she points at him and shouts to send for Mr. Smythe. Then, flustered, she corrects herself, telling Smythe to send for Mr. Smith. Smythe turns and quietly mutters, 'Double-strength,' as he exits. Mrs. Schuyler continues muttering in horror, repeating the newspaper headline, while Grayson follows behind, tapping the paper with a look of contempt.
related_events: Mrs. Schuyler reacts hysterically to the newspaper headline
Mrs. Schuyler gives confused instructions to the butler

name: Grayson Confronts Mrs. Schuyler with the Newspaper
description: Grayson rushes into the room holding a copy of the morning paper, his eyes blazing. He waves the paper and reads the headline aloud: "Cinderella Man Grows Hair On Chest!" His voice fills with contempt as he quotes James Braddock's statement: "I wear the pants," says Anne Schuyler's husband. Mrs. Schuyler, already agitated, turns to him and snaps, "Don't you think I know it, Grayson?" As Smythe the butler enters with a tray, she stammers, "Smith—send for Mr. Smythe! Er—Smythe, send for Mr. Smith!" Smythe nods and exits. Mrs. Schuyler mutters the headline under her breath as she paces away. Grayson follows close behind, repeating James's quote with scorn.
related_events: Grayson enters with the morning paper and confronts Mrs. Schuyler
Grayson mocks James Braddock's public statement

name: Stew and Anne Greet Acquaintances at the Gala
description: Stew and Anne move through the crowded roof apartment, surrounded by guests in evening dress. Anne approaches a small group and greets them by name: 'Hello, Natalie. Mr. Stewart Smith... Miss Montgomery, Mrs. Eames, Mrs. Radcliff, Mr. Radcliff.' Stew follows with a casual 'How-di-do.' The group murmurs polite acknowledgments as the sounds of conversation, laughter, and soft music fill the air.
related_events: Stew and Anne mingle with guests at the gala
Anne greets a group of acquaintances by name
Stew offers a casual greeting to the group
related_occasions: Evening Gala At The Roof Apartment

name: Whispers at the Gala
description: As Stew and Anne move through the crowd, pausing to exchange greetings with acquaintances, a cluster of women nearby watch them closely. One asks who Anne's companion is. Another replies that his name is Smith. The first woman scoffs, saying he can't be one of the brothers because he has no beard. Her friend remarks that he must have something to have caught Anne's attention. Nearby, Dexter Grayson stands in silence, taking a cocktail from a passing footman, his frown deepening as he watches the scene. At the grand piano, Mrs. Baxter bows toward a stout, swarthy Italian man with bristling mustachios, who returns the gesture with a deep bow. Polite applause spreads through the room as the young man at the piano begins to sing. Unnoticed, Stew and Anne turn away from the gathering and step quietly into the roof garden.

Dexter Grayson silently accepts a cocktail with disapproval
related_occasions: Evening Gala At The Roof Apartment

description: A piano chord rang out, drawing the guests' attention toward the grand piano. Mrs. Baxter stepped forward and gestured to the stout, swarthy Italian man with bristling mustachios who stood beside the piano. He bowed deeply, and she returned a graceful nod. Polite applause spread through the crowd as some guests took seats, settling in to listen. The young man at the piano began to sing.

Polite applause follows the introduction of the performers

name: Stew and Anne Slip Away to the Roof Garden
description: As the young man at the piano began to sing, the guests turned their attention toward the music, some settling into their seats. Amid the hush of the performance, Stew and Anne moved quietly through the room, stepping past the edge of the crowd. They passed through an opening in the wall and disappeared into the roof garden, leaving the glow and murmur of the gathering behind.
related_events: Stew and Anne quietly leave the room for the roof garden
related_occasions: Evening Gala At The Roof Apartment

name: Stew Welcomes the First Guests
description: Stew meets the butler Smythe in the hallway and tells him he will handle the door. He walks to the entrance and opens it, greeting Gallagher and Hank as they arrive. He greets them by name, invites them in, and offers them a drink.
related_events: Stew intercepts Smythe in the hallway
Stew opens the entrance door for Gallagher and Hank

name: Guests Arrive One After Another
description: Hank introduces Joe to Stew, who welcomes him. Joe steps inside and mentions that Johnson is waiting outside. Stew agrees to let Johnson in. Johnson enters and greets Stew warmly, then asks if he can bring in two friends who are nearby. Stew says it's all right. One by one, more people come through the door, filling the hallway and spilling into the rooms. As the group grows, Stew stands by the door, watching the crowd expand. Hank tells him the rest of the group will arrive later. Stew turns to Smythe and instructs him to take care of the guests and find out what those in the back room need.

Joe requests entry for Johnson
Johnson requests entry for two additional guests

name: Guests Flood Stew's Apartment
description: A group of 12 to 14 men and women entered Stew's apartment in single file, greeting him with cheerful hellos and handshakes as they passed by. They quickly spread into the hallway and moved into the rooms on either side, filling the space. Stew began to close the door, but before he could, several more guests pushed in, calling out greetings. The butler stood nearby, visibly stunned by the growing crowd. Stew watched in silence as the apartment filled with people.
related_events: Group of guests enters Stew's apartment in single file
Guests swarm into the hallway and spread into adjacent rooms
Additional guests enter while Stew attempts to close the door

name: Stew Hosts an Expanding Gathering
description: Stew opens the door to welcome Gallagher and Hank, who enter and are greeted warmly. Hank mentions he invited Joe along, and Stew agrees without hesitation. Joe steps in and calls for Johnson to join them, whom Stew also welcomes. As Johnson enters, he brings two more guests, and one by one, a growing crowd of men and women file in, greeting Stew with handshakes and cheerful hellos. Stew watches in silence as the hallway fills and the guests spill into adjacent rooms. When a few more arrive and push inside, Stew turns to Hank and remarks that he had been worried no one would come. Hank assures him the rest of the group will arrive later, as they are tied up with the morning edition. Stew, still uncertain, asks if they’re really coming, then calls out to Smythe, instructing him to serve drinks and check on the needs of those in the back room. Smythe, looking uneasy, is immediately pulled away by the guests before he can respond.
related_events: Stew expresses concern about low attendance to Hank
Hank explains delayed arrival of other guests
Stew instructs Smythe to manage the guests and check on the back room
Smythe is pulled away by the guests nervously

name: Stew Deals with Uninvited Guests
description: Stew confronts Gallagher about the uninvited guests who have arrived at his party, blaming him for the intrusion. Gallagher apologizes and explains that Hank was responsible for bringing them. Stew accepts the explanation and decides to handle the situation by instructing Smythe to serve the guests one drink and then remove them from the premises. As Smythe passes by, dazed and pushed along by revelers, Stew repeats the order, and Smythe nods in agreement. The party continues around them, loud and chaotic, as Stew turns his attention to other disruptions, including Bingy Baker’s comedic entrance in disguise, which briefly amuses him. After a physical joke involving a kick and a hidden bottle, Bingy joins the others in the drawing room. Stew remains in control, guiding Gallagher away from the entrance hall and up the stairs, the noise of the party filling the house.
related_events: Stew confronts Gallagher about bringing uninvited guests
Stew instructs Smythe to limit guests to one drink and then eject them

name: Bingy's Disguised Entrance and Reconciliation with Stew
description: Bingy pokes his head through the door wearing a false beard. Stew, spotting him, asks if there's a green elephant beside the guest. Bingy steps forward, revealing himself as little Bingy Baker. Stew rolls up his sleeves as if to throw a punch, but Bingy holds up a pair of glasses, pointing to them meaningfully. He enters cautiously, watching Stew, then strikes a pose and declares himself Big Chief Bingy, come to make peace. To show his remorse, he bends over and offers to let Stew kick him. Stew delivers a hard kick to his backside. Bingy straightens up, pulls a bottle of alcohol from his backside, and says the fire water is all right, then takes a drink. Both men laugh. Bingy says the matter is settled and expresses relief that Stew isn't truly angry, acknowledging that news is news. Stew agrees, calling Bingy's story a great one and saying he wishes he'd printed it. Bingy reminds him he gave him a break with the hairy chest story. Stew gestures to the false beard and notes it now reaches the chin. They both laugh. Stew tells Bingy to go into the other room for a drink. Bingy lets out a war whoop and heads into the drawing room, where Smythe is still surrounded by partygoers.

Stew prepares to punch Bingy but is deterred

name: Bingy's Mock Surrender and Reconciliation at Stew's Party
description: Bingy pokes his head through the doorway wearing a false beard. Stew, spotting him, pretends not to recognize him and asks if there's a green elephant nearby. Bingy steps in, removes his glasses, and strikes a pose, declaring himself Big Chief Bingy come to make peace with the white man. He bends over and offers to let Stew kick him where the sun never shines. Stew winds up and delivers a hard kick to Bingy's backside. Bingy straightens up stiffly, then pulls a bottle of alcohol from inside his clothing. He takes a swig and calls it fire water. Both men burst into laughter. Bingy says the matter is settled and expresses relief that Stew isn't truly angry, acknowledging that news is news. Stew agrees, calls the story a great one, and says he wishes he'd printed it. Bingy reminds him he gave him a break with the hairy chest story. Stew jokes about the false beard reaching up to the chin, then tells Bingy to go get a drink. Bingy lets out a war whoop and heads into the drawing room where the party continues.

Stew kicks Bingy in the backside as part of a ritualized reconciliation

Stew and Bingy reconcile and laugh together

name: Stew Welcomes Bingy Back at the Party
description: After a tense exchange marked by jokes and a playful kick, Stew relents and tells Bingy to go into the other room and get himself a drink. Bingy lets out a loud war-whoop, then heads into the drawing room where the party is still in full swing and Smythe remains overwhelmed by the guests.

Bingy lets out a war-whoop and enters the drawing room

name: Stew Threatens Gallagher Playfully at the Party
description: Stew looks at Gallagher and says he should punch him in the nose. Gallagher replies that he would love it. Smythe steps in, takes Gallagher by the arm, and leads him out of the entrance hall and upstairs, moving through the crowded, lively party.

description: Stew steps into the doorway of Mrs. Schuyler's home and pauses, met with a cold, silent glare from the jury, Mrs. Schuyler, and Anne. Dexter Grayson stands with his hands behind his back, watching Stew closely. Anne sits with tears in her eyes. Stew forces a smile, begins to whistle, and walks in. 'Good morning, everybody,' he says. No one answers. 'Well, maybe it isn't a good morning, huh?' He turns to Anne. 'Did you ever get the feeling that there was someone else in the room with you?' I didn't say it for publication, however.' Mrs. Schuyler demands to know if he struck the reporter in her house. 'Yes, I'm sorry, I struck him right here in your house. 'That's the fourteenth crack you've made to me. I'm keeping count. When you get to twenty, I'm gonna sock you right on the nose. As a matter of fact, I ought to sock you right now.' Mrs. Schuyler turns to Anne. 'Are you going to sit there and watch this man insult us? Haven't you any decency left?' Anne replies, 'Why doesn't Dexter show some decency? And you might show some too, Mother. What do you expect a man to do when he's called such names? I'm glad you hit that reporter, Stewart.' Mrs. Schuyler rises. 'All right, all right! It's your funeral, Anne Schuyler!' She leaves. Grayson starts to go, then turns. 'Cinderella Man!' Stew says, 'That's fifteen.' Grayson exits in a huff. Stew puts his arms around Anne as she cries.
